items.title: Interest rate rises likely in coming months, Bank of England’s chief economist says
items.summary: ‘We have further to go,’ says Huw Pill after increase to 4% last month as Bank seeks to tackle rising inflation The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said. items.title: Ukraine’s Starshield Access Is Being Restricted Again, Zelensky Says
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said the system, which Ukraine uses to guide drones, was being throttled over Russian-occupied territory. SpaceX, its developer, has denied the claim.

items.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage hits governments
items.summary: Tech company says operations restored to all customers and regions affected by one of worst IT failures in years Microsoft has said its service has been fully restored after a massive outage that saw widespread disruption to governments, businesses and public services around the world. The technology company said on Saturday morning it had restored service to the remaining customers affected by one of the worst IT failures in years. items.summary: The Ukrainian president says US envoys touted the exchange as part of efforts to end the war with Russia.

items.title: Greenpeace boulders may delay building of £12bn windfarms in North Sea
items.summary: Activists dumped rocks off Norfolk coast on site of Burnham-backed project in protest against seabed trawling The giant offshore windfarms backed by Andy Burnham this week may face unexpected stumbling blocks after Greenpeace activists unwittingly dumped about 15 tonnes of boulders on to the site as part of a campaign against seabed trawling in the North Sea. items.title: Torture survivors may have been sent to Sussex asylum camp unlawfully, documentary reveals
items.summary: Undercover ITV report also shows inadequate welfare checks at ex-military base run by firm of asylum camp billionaire Graham King Asylum seekers accommodated at a controversial military base in East Sussex have been subjected to inadequate welfare checks, and torture survivors may have been placed there unlawfully, a new undercover documentary for ITV has revealed. items.title: What’s Behind the Trump-Huang Relationship?
items.summary: President Trump’s show of support for Jensen Huang as he was under fire was a remarkable moment in a relationship that barely existed two years ago. Our White House correspondent Maggie Haberman explains how Mr. Trump came to see Mr. Huang as a modern-day Henry Ford.

items.title: Hosting Ex-Convicts at Their Oakland Home Has Largely Gone Off Without a Hitch
items.summary: A couple in Oakland, Calif., has welcomed into their home 24 men recently released from prison sentences for violent crimes, part of a program to ease reintegration into society.

items.title: Hundreds of children in England prescribed weight-loss jabs, figures show
items.summary: Exclusive: investigation finds prescriptions for children under 12, as experts stress need for specialist supervision and long-term monitoring Hundreds of children in England are receiving prescriptions for GLP-1 medications, including some younger than 12, the Guardian can reveal. GLP-1 medications were initially developed to help people with type 2 diabetes control their blood sugar levels, but have since become a popular slimming aid, with products such as Wegovy and Mounjaro becoming household names. items.summary: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

items.title: A ‘Generational Clash’ Is Fueling Europe’s Protests
items.summary: As retirees live longer, governments need to spend more on pensions. That makes it harder to fund other services, spurring protests like those planned this weekend in France.

items.title: Two Celebrity Cases Put a Spotlight on British Courts’ Gag Orders
items.summary: Russell Brand and the TV personality David Walliams both persuaded courts to suppress misconduct allegations against them. Some say the libel laws need to change.
